chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan and others, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Ribat, from Yunus ibn 'Ammar, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the wudu for the salat, so he said: 'Once, once'.
ai.seo_question: What is the minimum requirement for wudu before performing salat according to this narration?
ai.summary: This concise narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the foundational minimum requirement for ablution, emphasizing that a single wash of the face and hands suffices for validity unless specific conditions necessitate repetition. It reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle of adhering to the literal text of the Quran while allowing for scholarly elaboration on recommended acts (mustahabbat) and detailed procedures found in other traditions. The brevity of the answer highlights the direct link between the ritual act and the divine command in Surah al-Ma'idah.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Al Hassan, and someone else, from sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Rabaat, from Yunus Bin Ammar who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the Ablution (Wudhu) for the Salaat, so heasws said: ‘(Washing the face) once, (washing the hands) once’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn al-Hassan and others have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn Mahbub from ibn Ribat from Yunus ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:
“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about Wudu’ for Salah (prayer). He (the Imam) said, ‘It is (washing the face) once and (hands) once.’”
